result.summary: No ship. The per-session quarantine closes the three round-2 halt failures, but its trigger still misses a valid request shape and can permanently mark a request-less projection as processed.

findings.title: A/HEAVY — Table G misses array-content requests
findings.body: G1 treats a `user` role in `gateExtract.messages` as proof that the raw session contained a request. For Claude array-content records, the raw parser emits only `tool_result` messages, not a `user` message (`src/core/transcripts/claude.js:153-171`). If such a record contains the person's text and a later Claude Code version changes `promptSource`, Table H declines it; G1 then sees a reply but no user role in either extract. The collector admits the session and can mark it processed, permanently losing that request from the dream. The spec acknowledges array-content prompts but relies on the measured files also having string-content records; that does not hold for an array-only session.
findings.recommendation: Carry a text-free, pre-cap indication that a parsed Claude record contained a request-shaped string or text block, and use it for G1. Add an array-only request with a declined source field to the collector and mixed-night tests. This changes Table G and its Deliverables.

next_steps: Apply the pinned round-3 HEAVY-finding rule: re-cut to candidate 0 and take Tables H and G together to the owner.
